name: Down by Law
label: Epitaph
lede: [[Dave Smalley]] had already sung for [[DYS]], [[Dag Nasty]] and [[ALL]] when he started a fourth band in Los Angeles. [[Brett Gurewitz]] signed it after a talk in his car, and a punk take on a Proclaimers hit got it onto MTV.

eras.title: A Boston singer, a Los Angeles band
eras.text: Dave Smalley had already fronted DYS, Dag Nasty and ALL when he started writing songs that fit none of them. In Los Angeles he found guitarist Chris Bagarozzi, bassist Ed Urlik and drummer Dave Naz.

years.src: No Echo · Wikipedia: Down by Law
years.h: Still in ALL, Smalley writes "Right or Wrong" on a 4-track
years.p: He called drummer Dave Naz to jam on it, then added guitarist Chris Bagarozzi and bassist Ed Urlik. Down by Law was a Los Angeles band with a Boston singer.
years.xp:
Smalley told No Echo he wrote "Right or Wrong" on a Tascam 4-track while he was still in [[ALL|e92547b5-a134-4149-af9a-c944af9e476f]], then called Naz to play on it. He kept writing songs before the band played live.

Wikipedia dates the band to 1989 and lists Smalley, Bagarozzi, Urlik and Naz as the original four.

years.h: The Anti-Club in Hollywood hosts the first show
years.p: Down by Law plays its first show on March 10, 1990, with Smalley, Bagarozzi, Urlik and Naz.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives the date and the room. Smalley had left ALL as the band formed, so this was the first time the Boston singer fronted a Los Angeles lineup in front of a crowd.

eras.title: Gurewitz at the board, twice
eras.text: Brett Gurewitz of Bad Religion signed the band to Epitaph and produced its first two albums. The original lineup came apart soon after the second.

years.big: "Brett brought us out to his car to talk and the next thing I knew Down by Law was on Epitaph."
years.h: Brett Gurewitz signs them after one early show
years.p: Smalley, to No Echo, on how the Bad Religion guitarist and Epitaph founder got the band. It was 1991.

years.h: Gurewitz produces Down by Law, with "Surf Punk" on it
years.p: Twelve songs in about 35 minutes, among them "Right or Wrong" and "American Dream." Urlik wrote the music for "Surf Punk."
years.xp: Smalley wrote most of the record. Naz wrote "The Truth," and "Best Friends" is a cover of a song by The Outlets.

years.h: A year later, Blue, and Gurewitz again
years.p: Gurewitz produces the second album as he did the first. The original four tour behind it, then leave.

yt: Full set at Emo's, Houston, December 7, 1992
years.h: Three founders leave, and Smalley is the last one standing
years.p: Bagarozzi, Urlik and Naz go after the tour for Blue. Wikipedia lists Mark Phillips and Pat Hoed as brief replacements in 1993 and 1994.
years.xp: The clip is the original four at Emo's in Houston on December 7, 1992, the lineup that made the first two albums. The "D.C. Guns" EP dates from 1993.

eras.title: Punkrockacademyfightsong
eras.text: Sam Williams, "Angry" John DiMambro and Hunter Oswald joined Smalley, and the album they made became the one the band is best known for.

years.h: Sam Williams, "Angry" John DiMambro and Hunter Oswald join Smalley
years.p: Williams plays guitar, DiMambro bass and Oswald drums. It is the second lineup, and the one that records Punkrockacademyfightsong.

years.h: Punkrockacademyfightsong turns a Proclaimers hit into a punk song
years.p: Michael W. Douglass produced it at A&M Studios in Hollywood: 19 tracks in 46 minutes, two of them interludes of 5 and 27 seconds. It is generally cited as the band's best seller.
years.xp:
The album includes a punk take on The Proclaimers' "I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)," which got MTV and radio play, as did the video for "Hit or Miss."

Smalley told No Echo: "There was an unspoken electricity happening while we made Punkrockacademyfightsong."

Reviews split. AllMusic called it "a solid, polished album of raw punk rock," the Boston Herald "fast and loud, yet marvelously melodic," and the Chicago Reader "punk as pabulum."

years.cap: Smalley on guitar at Local 186, Boston, 1994
years.h: The Rolling Stones, in the same studio, allegedly complain about the volume
years.p: Wikipedia says both bands were at A&M Studios at the same time during the Punkrockacademyfightsong sessions.

eras.title: On the road, then off Epitaph
eras.text: Down by Law toured behind Epitaph labelmates, made two more albums for the label, and in 1998 moved to Go-Kart.

yt: Mind Melt Video special, shot March 25, 1995
years.h: Smalley tours full time and studies at Cal State Los Angeles
years.p: He fits three-month tours into the school's quarter system, and in 1995 his oldest daughter is born in Southern California.
years.xp: Smalley told No Echo the master's degree took about six years. Becoming a father shifted his priorities on the road.

years.h: All Scratched Up! comes out as Oswald's first stint ends
years.p: The fourth album, still on Epitaph. Wikipedia lists Danny Westman on drums in 1996 and 1997, then Chris Lagerborg through 1999.

years.h: Epitaph gets one more: Last of the Sharpshooters
years.p: It is Down by Law's last record for the label it joined in 1991.

years.h: Down by Law opens for NOFX, the Offspring, Pennywise and Bad Religion
years.p: Wikipedia gives the 1990s as the span, not a single tour.

years.h: Down by Law moves to Go-Kart Records
years.p: The label it joined in 1991 gets no more albums; Fly the Flag comes out on Go-Kart.

years.h: DiMambro and Lagerborg leave after Fly the Flag
years.p: The band's one album for Go-Kart Records. Bassist John DiMambro and drummer Chris Lagerborg are gone soon after.

eras.title: New players, a death, a pause
eras.text: The lineup turned over again, the label changed again, and in 2003 the band went quiet.

years.h: Milo Todesco takes the drums for a split with Pseudo Heroes
years.p: Keith Davies is on bass for the 2000 split release, after the Fly the Flag departures.

years.h: Former drummer Chris Lagerborg dies in his sleep at 33
years.p: He had played drums for Down by Law from 1997 to 1999, and Wikipedia gives 2002 as the year.

years.h: A new label, Union 2112, and Windwardtidesandwaywardsails
years.p: The band signed to Union 2112 in December 2002 and released the album in May 2003.

years.h: Then it goes quiet for five years
years.p: A hiatus begins later in 2003 and runs until Smalley restarts the band in 2008.

eras.title: Smalley restarts it, and 1994 comes back
eras.text: Smalley restarted the band in 2008, and by 2017 the lineup from Punkrockacademyfightsong was together again.

years.h: Smalley restarts the band with a new song, "Bullets"
years.p: It is August 2008, five years after the hiatus began.

years.cap: Smalley with Williams behind him, JohnBull, Curitiba, Brazil, May 14, 2009
years.src: Flickr: Dave & Sam · Wikipedia: Down by Law
years.h: The comeback tour starts in South America
years.p: Down by Law's first tour since 2003 plays Brazil and other South American dates, plus some shows in the US.
years.xp: The Curitiba show in the photo was the band's first there in nine years, according to the fan review it came from. Smalley and Williams are the two members of the 1994 lineup on stage.

years.cap: Smalley at Coney Island High, New York, July 8, 2011
years.h: Champions at Heart is the first full album of the comeback
years.p: Released on DC Jam in 2012, it is the first full-length since the 2003 hiatus.

years.cap: Smalley after a solo acoustic show at Goldmark's, Stuttgart, May 30, 2016
years.h: DiMambro and Oswald come back, and 1994 is whole again
years.p: John DiMambro on bass and Hunter Oswald on drums rejoin Smalley and Williams, the lineup behind Punkrockacademyfightsong.

years.h: The 1994 lineup makes All In
years.p: It follows the 2017 return of DiMambro and Oswald and puts all four on one record again.

years.h: Lonely Town follows in 2021
years.p: It is the second album from the reunited lineup, three years after All In.

years.h: Crazy Days arrives July 12, 2024
years.p: The band's newest album, from the same four members who reunited in 2017.
